newsitem.title: USA: U.S. natgas supplies ample for winter, AGA says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. natgas supplies ample for winter, AGA says.

text.p: U.S supplies of natural gas appear ample for the winter heating season, with total available volume estimated at 2,659 billion cubic feet, American Gas Association said Wednesday.
"That exceeds by 117 Bcf the historic peak month consumption level set in January 1994. So, supply availability is unlikely to be a problem," AGA president Michael Baly said in a statement.

According to an AGA analysis, restructuring of the natural gas industry and unbundling of a variety of industry services likely has enhanced the process of supplying gas to customers at competitive prices.

"During the first seven months of 1996, residential prices reported by the U.S. Department of Energy were on average only two pennies higher than during the first seven months of 1995, even though the price of gas at the wellhead was up by 62 cents," Baly said.

"In real terms, average residential prices have declined nearly 28 percent since 1985. This was made possible by lower local distribution company costs and productivity improvements throughout the natural gas industry," he said.
